profile.summary: FRIGID generates candidate molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum (de novo structure elucidation). A MIST encoder predicts a molecular fingerprint from the spectrum, and a masked diffusion language model generates molecules as SAFE strings conditioned on that fingerprint and the chemical formula. An optional refinement loop simulates spectra of the candidates with the ICEBERG forward model and re-generates the parts that do not match.

summary_quotes.text: **FRIGID** is a diffusion language model (DLM) framework for *de novo* structural elucidation from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS).

Given an observed spectrum, FRIGID generates molecular structures as SAFE sequences conditioned on intermediate fingerprint representations and chemical formulae, with optional iterative refinement guided by a forward fragmentation model (ICEBERG).

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Stage 1 (FRIGID-base): a MIST encoder predicts a 4096-bit radius-2 Morgan fingerprint; its active bits are embedded and passed through 3 self-attention layers, and the precursor formula is encoded as per-element counts; both enter every Transformer block through cross-attention. The backbone is a 12-layer BERT-style masked diffusion language model (hidden size 896, 14 heads) over BPE-tokenised SAFE strings, and an NGBoost model predicts the sequence length from the formula. Stage 2: candidates are ranked against the predicted fingerprint, ICEBERG simulates their spectra, peaks that appear in simulation but not in the experiment flag inconsistent atoms, and those tokens are re-masked and re-denoised over several rounds. The code is adapted from NVIDIA's GenMol.

quotes.text: MIST encoder predicts a 4096-bit radius-2 Morgan fingerprint from the spectrum. Active bit indices are embedded and processed through 3 self-attention layers, then injected via cross-attention into every Transformer block.

The model evaluated in the paper uses a 12-layer BERT Transformer (hidden size 896, 14 heads, FFN dimension 3072)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README reports that earlier MIST encoders for MassSpecGym were trained with synthetic spectra of PubChem molecules chosen to resemble test formulas, which used test-set information. The encoders were replaced (MIST 2M-aug for NPLIB1, MIST 4M-aug for MassSpecGym), the evaluations repeated, and the earlier results marked as superseded: for example FRIGID on MassSpecGym fell from 18.29% to 9.05% top-1 accuracy. The updated release (Zenodo record 23543494, 2026-10-21, Apache 2.0) holds DLM.ckpt and four ICEBERG checkpoints; MIST encoders come from a separate Zenodo record. The paper read is arXiv v3 (25 Oct 2026). A result should state which MIST encoder was used, whether refinement was applied and how many rounds.

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: MassSpecGym in the Wild (an existing source on this record) lists FRIGID in its updated MassSpecGym de novo leaderboard with 18.29% top-1 accuracy, the figure the FRIGID README now marks as previous and superseded, and also evaluates FRIGID for generative retrieval. For its own augmentation experiments it trained MIST encoders with a modified MIST implementation that it links to the MIST-FRIGID branch of the FRIGID repository.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Conditional generative model: masked diffusion language model for de novo molecule generation from MS/MS, with optional forward-model-guided refinement.

quotes.text: A masked diffusion language model (MDLM) that generates SAFE molecular strings conditioned on predicted Morgan fingerprints (via MIST) and chemical formulae (via cross-attention).

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 12-layer BERT MDLM (d=896, 14 heads) with cross-attention to fingerprint and formula encoders; MIST fingerprint encoder; NGBoost length model; ICEBERG forward model for refinement.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Decoder pretraining on up to 230 million unlabeled structures as SAFE sequences (datamol-io/safe-gpt on Hugging Face), with test and validation InChIKeys excluded. MIST and ICEBERG are trained on the NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym training splits; the revised MIST encoders also use GLACIER spectra for 2 million sampled PubChem molecules or the official 4 million MassSpecGym molecules.

run_guide.summary: Install FRIGID with its ICEBERG submodule, download the benchmark data and checkpoints, train a token-length model and run the MassSpecGym benchmark with FRIGID-base.
prerequisites: A GPU (the authors timed inference on an NVIDIA 6000 Ada).
wget and about 2.6 GB for the checkpoint archive, plus the MIST encoders and benchmark data.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/coleygroup/FRIGID.git
cd FRIGID
git checkout --detach 5adba44b643e444b5b28e54645ce8dde11df2437
git submodule update --init --recursive
steps.explanation: The README's clone command has a placeholder URL; Rewire filled in the repository URL and added the checkout line to pin the reviewed commit.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda create -n frigid python=3.10
conda activate frigid
bash env/patch_ms_pred.sh
pip install -r ms-pred/requirements.txt
pip install -e ./ms-pred
pip install -e .
steps.explanation: As the README gives it, including the ms-pred patch.
